title: Revisiting Computation for Research: Practices and Trends
problem: An understanding gap exists between providers of computational resources and researchers who depend on them. Research computing practices have evolved significantly over the past decade and require systematic re-examination to reflect current trends and emerging challenges.
motivation: Understanding how researchers utilize computational resources is critical for designing effective computational systems and infrastructure investments that meet evolving research needs.
method: The study revisits questions from a prior decade-old survey through over 100 interviews and uses quantitative comparison of past and present results. Qualitative analysis employs large language models to extract insights and patterns from interview transcripts. A methodological toolkit is developed for future assessment of the research computing landscape.
key_novelty: Longitudinal revisitation of research computing practices over a decade, augmented with LLM-assisted qualitative analysis to systematically identify emerging trends in how researchers utilize computational resources.
contributions: Systematic survey of 100+ research computing practitioners bridging resource provider and user perspectives
Quantitative and qualitative analysis revealing trends and challenges in contemporary research computation
Methodological toolkit for ongoing assessment and monitoring of the research computing landscape
Evidence-based recommendations for enhancing computational systems and resource allocation strategies

metrics.other: survey-based qualitative and quantitative analysis of 100+ interviews

limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed in abstract; potential concerns include survey respondent selection bias and generalizability across research domains.
primary_theme: Evolution of research computing practices and infrastructure
